content:
maria: Quick follow-up to the canary RFC — I sketched a lightweight fallback shim idea that avoids full traffic escrow. Idea: when A-arm shows early degradation we mirror a small percentage to B-arm (shadow) and then, on threshold, reroute live requests through B while keeping A warm as a fallback. Want thoughts on interfaces, operator handoff, and costs. :thinking:

prashant: High-level sounds good. Two quick q's: how do we keep session affinity when we switch? and what's the signal surface — latency p95, error rate, model score drop?

maria: Good q's. Session affinity: keep sticky token that maps to chosen variant; update mapping atomically during switch. Signal surface: primary = 5xx rate and p95; secondary = model quality regression signal (eval latency + metric delta). We also need a "soft switch" path to avoid IO thundering when many sessions flip simultaneously.

olivia: Soft switch = ramp over window + per-tenant concurrency cap? Also consider prefix cache priming cost if B has different kv-layout / quantization. If B is quantized variant, cold-cache token cost may spike.

leo: Agree with olivia. Operator handoff: provide a small CLI / console knob with three states: observe -> soft-divert -> hard-divert. Each state maps to routing percentages and warmup orchestration. Operators can abort to observe.

maria: Thinking of a tiny policy DSL for the knob, e.g.:
```
policy:
  mode: soft-divert
  duration: 5m
  ramp: linear
  start_pct: 5
  end_pct: 60
  tie_break: prefer-low-latency
```
This stays in control plane and runtime consumes ephemeral lease.

prashant: Nice. A few implementation-level tradeoffs:
- Where to evaluate signals? Centralized observer vs local agent. Centralized makes consistent decisions but adds commit latency. Local agent faster but may diverge across cells.
- How to ensure rollback safety if B degrades in a different way? Need dual-signal: B-specific health + end-to-end user-facing SLO.

olivia: For divergence: add quorum on observer decisions across region observers, or require N-of-M agreement before hard-divert. Also include a probe that sends synthetic golden prompts to both variants to capture quality regressions earlier.

leo: Also add circuit budget: how many distinct tenants can be actively failing over concurrently, to avoid capacity exhaustion on B. We should expose per-tenant budget and global budget.

maria: Good point. Cost tradeoff: keeping A warm costs GPU memory and KV cache; spinning up new B replicas costs burst-capacity. We can optimize by keeping a minimal number of A workers in standby and spin additional B workers only if ramp passes a threshold.

prashant: Ops/visibility: need token-level traces showing which variant served each request + a route history per token (to diagnose flapping). Add a per-request header: X-variant-id and record in request span.

maria: Agreed. Also want an operator runbook snippet for common scenarios:
1) p95 spikes, 2) small increase in 5xx, 3) model-quality drift detected.
Runbook (abridged):
- On p95 spike: check kernel-level stats -> if KV miss rate > 0.3, start soft-divert to warmed B.
- On 5xx burst: if >= 0.5% for 2m, hard-divert but keep A as fallback.
- On model-quality drift: gate on golden-probe delta > threshold for 3 minutes before hard-divert.

sre-oncall: Add automated alerts that surface "divert-in-progress" and allow quick rollback via slack slash command. Also require a human ack for cross-region hard-diverts.

deploy-bot: deploy-notes: added runtime flags --fallback-mode --fallback-lease-ttl. Example rollout CLI: `ri rollout --policy-id=soft-hedge-42 --dry-run`

olivia: Edge-case: prefix caching — if we flip many sessions simult, cache miss storm can double token cost. Mitigate with staggered ramp by token hash buckets.

leo: Suggestion: use probabilistic hedging during ramp (small fraction double-proxied to both variants) to build warm caches on B without redirecting all traffic. Then gradually shift primary. That reduces cold-cache spike.

maria: Love the probabilistic double-proxy. Also a note on interface boundaries: control-plane policy DSL vs runtime enforcement must be minimal — policy only expresses intent (mode/ramp/guards); runtime decides exact percentages per shard to meet capacity constraints. That keeps operator UX simple.

prashant: Final thought: we should codify safety invariants: max-cost-multiplier, max-concurrent-diverts, and required telemetry before hard-divert. Add these to policy as optional constraints.

maria: Great comments — I'll turn this into an RFC follow-up doc with a small state-machine diagram and a draft DSL. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
